posts.headline: Thicks and the #FreeMaxx Champions finally get to draft instead of just talking about it, and a 14-14 career record with a 5.5 average finish means the ring still owes this league a real résumé.
posts.detail: Two seasons, one title, and a career mark that's dead even at 14-14 — the pedigree says contender, the numbers say prove it, and tonight's draft board is the last excuse left.

posts.headline: Put it in Ra owns the single best résumé in Busters Anonymous history — 20-8, a 1.5 average finish, back-to-back top-two seasons — and somehow zero rings and zero words to show for it.
posts.detail: One Nut Barner has let this column run an entire month unanswered while sitting on a .714 win percentage with no championship; that gap between production and hardware is the loudest silence in the league.

posts.headline: talentedtenthh drafts tonight still holding the worst résumé in the league — a 4-10 record and a dead-last 12th-place finish — and nothing suggests Chauncey suddenly discovered a war room over the offseason.
posts.detail: A 0.286 win percentage and a 12th-place finish in year one is the floor of this league; the untalented tenth nickname wrote itself and tonight's draft is the first chance to erase it.

posts.headline: Sasinci's World finally sits at the draft table with zero editions of stonewalling left, and Big Head still hasn't explained how a championship banner hangs over a losing 13-15 career record.
posts.detail: A title and a losing record don't usually coexist, but Alxgalvn has pulled it off across two seasons and a 5.5 average finish — tonight's picks either justify the fluke jury or convict it.

posts.headline: SwooshAnoosh enters draft night with the worst win percentage in the entire league and nobody's expecting the Prince of Persia to suddenly reign over anything.
posts.detail: A 5-9 rookie campaign capped by an 11th-place finish and a .357 win percentage is about as bottom-feeder as it gets — the only mystery left is how much worse it can get from here.
